# VoidSailors: Where Truth Lies

> VoidSailors: Where Truth Lies is a fantasy GameLit novel for young adults by E. J. Perry. Players crew hover-sail ships through a five-day in-game contest across islands floating above the Great Deep, where four factions bargain, supplies run short, death is permanent and there are no second runs. Progress comes from trust, attention and the price of each alliance rather than from stats.

- Author: E. J. Perry
- Genre: GameLit, fantasy, young adult
- Format: print and digital
- Release: coming soon to Amazon (date to be announced)
- ISBN: 979-8-89170-595-1
- Language: English
- Tagline: Five days. Four factions. No second runs.

## Pages

- [Home](https://voidsailors.com/): the premise, the four factions, the five days of the contest, the main characters, the world and the author
- [The Book](https://voidsailors.com/book.html): overview, genre and style, systems and mechanics, the world and publication details
- [Read a Free Chapter](https://voidsailors.com/sample.html): "Appointment in the Storm", a complete free chapter (about a 7-minute read)
- [Triage by the Gate](https://voidsailors.com/gate.html): a seven-question quiz that sorts the reader into a faction

## The four factions

- Pirates: independence and freedom
- C.A.T.s (Corporate Alliance of Trade): traders
- Socialists: direction, unity and efficiency
- Nomads: every man for himself

## The five days

1. The Sign in the Ruins
2. The Taste of Freedom
3. Nothing You Can Take
4. The Warmth of Strangers
5. The Shorter Crossing

## Protagonist

TenScore, played by Dexter Blackwell, is a young man who answers fear with a joke. He sets out from the Armada Gate on foot, wearing the colors of a faction he never picked, and every crew that takes him aboard hands him a new name.

## Characters

- Three Abreast, the three who change his course: Moss (Sage of the Unlit Pipe), Tim (Asker of Plain Questions), Pebbles (Keeper of the Lore)
- Crew and rivals: OnJee, the Gatekeeper, Spag, Älys, Markus Dark, Blue, Axer Justice

## The author

E. J. Perry writes GameLit that trades stats for consequence inside broken systems. The novel carries its philosophy under the surface: higher powers, justice and the systems people live in are argued by characters, never preached. It is written for readers tired of stat sheets and level-ups.
